Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

like preposition

similar to, in the manner of

also just like, as (like), as if, the size of, look like

classical

Cic. Sen. 44: hominēs capiantur ut piscēs

ut, sīcut

adverbs of comparison; the noun after them takes the case of the word it is compared with

like, as

The plain “like” of a comparison: ut piscēs, like fish.

Other words

  • tamquam, velut — like, just as; as if

    adverbs of comparison; before a clause, with the subjunctive (“as if”) · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor; Quint. 6.3.59: tamquam assem elephantō dēs

  • īnstar + gen. — like, as big as, the size of

    indeclinable noun, with the genitive · also used · classical · Catull. 17.12: puerī īnstar bimulī; Verg. A. 2.15: īnstar montis equum

    Properly “the likeness, the size”: īnstar montis, as big as a mountain.

  • similis, simile — like, similar to

    adjective, third declension, with the genitive or the dative · also used · classical · Liv. 26.50.13: dīs simillimum juvenem; Mt. 7.26: similis erit virō stultō

    When “like” follows be or look; see similar. Unlike: dissimilis (see different).

Examples

  • dīvīnē enim Platō ‘ēscam malōrum’ appellat voluptātem, quod eā vidēlicet hominēs capiantur ut piscēs

    for Plato, inspired, calls pleasure “the bait of evils”, because men are caught by it like fishCic. Sen. 44

  • ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

    I talk to you as I talk to myselfCic. Att. 8.14.2

  • puerī īnstar bimulī tremulā patris dormientis in ulnā

    like a little boy of two asleep in his father’s rocking armCatull. 17.12–13

  • tum sēmen seritō crēbrum tamquam līnum, eō terram crībrō incernitō altam digitum trānsversum

    then sow the seed thick, like flax, and sift earth over it a finger’s breadth deepCato Agr. 48.1

  • mūtāta omnia altōque cinere tamquam nive obducta

    everything was changed, and covered in deep ash, as if with snowPlin. Ep. 6.20.18

  • nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs

    “Don’t hold it out,” he said, “as if you were giving a penny to an elephant”Quint. 6.3.59

  • similis erit virō stultō, quī aedificāvit domum suam super arēnam

    he will be like a foolish man who built his house upon the sandMt. 7.26

See also similar, different, same.
